items: Emission sources: burning wood and fossil fuels raises local pollution; factories and power plants release SOx and NOx, vehicles release CO, PM and VOCs.
Meteorological conditions: wind, temperature and humidity affect the dispersion and concentration of pollutants; a layer of warm air trapping pollutants near the ground can cause poor air quality.
Natural events: wildfires release large amounts of smoke and PM; dust storms can lower air quality significantly.
Seasonal changes: heating or cooling of buildings in different seasons increases emissions, and seasonal pollen adds to poor air quality.
